_comment: Classification rules for the signin / payment / transaction SMS channels.
sms_parser.py reloads this file when its mtime changes, so a provider that
changes its wording or separators can be handled by editing this file and
restarting the workers — no code change, no redeploy.
brands: matched against the message body first, then against the sender
address (which the SMS forwarder posts as `sender`). A brand decides the
family; the first matching entry wins, so keep the most specific first.
keywords.otp: a message needs one of these plus an extractable code before
it can be an OTP at all. Add wording here when a provider changes it.
keywords.signin: sign-in vocabulary, used when the sender/brand is unknown.
keywords.payment: payment vocabulary. A wallet's OTP may name only the
merchant ("OTP for PAYMENT ... to IVAC"), so this plus a wallet sender
is what tells a payment OTP from a sign-in one.
keywords.warning: security-warning wording. An OTP keyword inside one of
these clauses is not an OTP announcement — wallets print the same line on
transaction SMS, where it would otherwise be read as the OTP.
trx_anchors: the labels a transaction ID follows. The token right after the
anchor is read as the TRX ID.
senders: sender addresses (wallet shortcodes, gateway numbers) mapped to a
brand. The forwarder posts the SMS sender address, so this is what labels
messages whose body never names the provider — a Rocket transaction, for
example, only says "Tk4,500.00 paid ... TxnId:". Keys are compared
case-insensitively and, for numeric addresses, digit for digit after
dropping a 880 country code. Add a new shortcode here; routing is decided
by the body whenever the body names a brand.
